title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP wait-on-send support
summary: The roadmap facts and documented commands are supported, and the briefing correctly separates planned Mac behaviour from existing Windows controls. Minor corrections should complete the admin paths, acknowledge the general DLP licensing requirement, and flag conflicting troubleshooting guidance about Mac policy tips.

claims.quote: Outlook for Mac will support Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) wait-on-send policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the Mac wait-on-send default or what happens on arrival.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Learn does not yet document the Mac wait-on-send implementation or its controlling setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send default licensing timeout configuration; Outlook Mac wait on send DLP license price meter roles version. Opened mobile, new Outlook and classic Outlook DLP references, Set-OrganizationConfig and Mac preferences; no Mac implementation.

claims.claim: The dlpwaitonsendtimeout registry key configures wait on send for Outlook for Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: After you've configured the Oversharing dialog, you can optionally enable the **Wait on send** dialog feature using the *dlpwaitonsendtimeout Registry key (DWORD value)*.

claims.claim: Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content is the documented Group Policy setting for that registry-based wait.
claims.quote: You can set this *RegKey* via group policy, **Specify wait time to evaluate sensitive content**, script, or other mechanism for configuring registry keys.

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled controls pre-send DLP evaluation in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: **DLPWaitOnSendEnabled***boolean*: true or false.**Default**: false When true, it enables evaluation of the mail for Data loss prevention before mail is sent.

claims.claim: DLPWaitOnSendTimeout controls how long new Outlook waits before offering an override.
claims.quote: The DLPWaitOnSendTimeout parameter specifies how long in seconds Outlook for Windows waits for data loss prevention (DLP) evaluation to complete on a new message before offering an override.

claims.claim: The mobile policy-tip reference says Android and iOS do not yet support DLP wait to send.
claims.quote: Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support *DLP Wait‑to‑Send

claims.claim: That reference's wait-on-send section names Android and iOS rather than macOS.
claims.quote:
## Wait on send dialog support for oversharing

Outlook for Android and iOS doesn't yet support *DLP Wait‑to‑Send

claims.claim: For the documented Outlook for Microsoft 365 registry setting, an unconfigured wait sends the message immediately.
claims.quote: When *dlpwaitonsendtimeout* isn't configured, the message isn't checked before the user sends it. The email message is sent immediately once **Send** is clicked.

claims.claim: In that unconfigured case, DLP evaluates the sent message and applies policy actions afterwards.
claims.quote: The email message is sent immediately once **Send** is clicked. The DLP data classification service evaluates the message and apply the actions defined in the DLP policy.

claims.claim: For Outlook for Microsoft 365, a configured wait from 0 to 9999 seconds offers Send anyway if evaluation has not completed.
claims.quote: If the policy evaluation doesn't complete in the specified time a **Send anyway** button appears allowing the user to bypass the presend check. The **T** value range is 0 to 9999 seconds.

claims.claim: For that registry-based configuration, values greater than 9999 are replaced with 10000.
claims.quote: If the **T** value is greater than 9999, it's replaced with 10000

claims.claim: Those registry values above 9999 hold the message until evaluation completes without a Send Anyway override.
claims.quote: the **Send Anyway** button doesn't appear. This holds the message until the policy evaluation completes and doesn't provide the user with an *override* option.

claims.claim: A timeout of zero shows Send Anyway immediately in new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: When DLPWaitOnSendTimeout = 0, user will immediately see “Send Anyway” in the infobar of mail.

claims.claim: Whether Mac offers the same timeout bypass is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send default licensing timeout configuration. Opened dlp-outlook-mobile-policy-tip-ref, dlp-policy-reference-new-outlook, dlp-osp-get-started and Set-OrganizationConfig; override descriptions do not establish Mac behaviour.

claims.claim: Matching DLP block rules block the message regardless of the Policy tips configuration.
claims.quote: If the block rules defined in the DLP policy are met, the message will be blocked regardless of how **Policy tips** is configured.

claims.claim: In the documented Outlook for Microsoft 365 experience, evaluation duration varies with internet speed, content length and policy count.
claims.quote: The duration for completing the evaluation can vary depending on factors such as internet speed, content length, and the number of policies defined.

claims.claim: Policy-tip UI is off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS and macOS until its Microsoft 365 Apps policy is enabled.
claims.quote: Policy Tip UI is turned off by default in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS to allow for administrators to test and perform user training prior to deployment.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published an entitlement specific to Mac wait on send.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac Purview DLP wait on send licensing E5 pricing default administrator. Opened Microsoft Purview service description and Mac/mobile, Windows and classic Outlook DLP references; general DLP entitlements are published, but no Mac wait-on-send-specific entitlement.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included under the standard's product-level licensing rule. Add to licensing.notes and the licensing paragraph: 'Exchange Online DLP requires an eligible licence, such as Microsoft 365 E3 or E5; Microsoft has not published a requirement specific to Mac wait on send.' The already cited Microsoft Purview service description lists those general DLP entitlements. Retain the caveat against assuming the Windows oversharing requirements apply to Mac.

claims.claim: The documented pre-send oversharing configuration uses a DLP policy scoped to Exchange.
claims.quote: To enable these pop-ups, first scope your policy to the Exchange location and then select the **Show policy tip as a dialog for the user before send** option

claims.claim: The documented DLP rule option is Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only).
claims.quote: Select **Policy tips** > **Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only)**.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -DLPWaitOnSendEnabled $true -DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <seconds> is a documented Exchange Online organisation control.
claims.quote:
[-DLPWaitOnSendEnabled <Boolean>]
[-DLPWaitOnSendTimeout <Int16>]

$true: Mail sent from Outlook for Windows to Exchange is evaluated by DLP.

A valid value is an integer from 0 to 9999.

claims.claim: Learn documents no admin-centre UI path for the Exchange wait-to-send parameters.
claims.quote: Searched: DLPWaitOnSendEnabled DLPWaitOnSendTimeout admin center UI Set-OrganizationConfig. Opened Set-OrganizationConfig and dlp-policy-reference-new-outlook; the latter says the experience is controlled solely through the Exchange parameters, with no UI path.

claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send default licensing timeout configuration; DLPWaitOnSendEnabled DLPWaitOnSendTimeout admin center UI Set-OrganizationConfig. Opened the parameter reference and mobile/new Outlook references; their documented parameter reach does not include Mac.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path Customization > Policy Management reaches the policy-tips policy management area.
claims.quote: You can access this policy under **Customization** and **Policy Management**.
claims.fix: The path stops at the policy list. Extend it to 'Customization > Policy Management > Create > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook > Enabled'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/admin-center/overview-cloud-policy alongside the mobile policy-tip reference for the creation steps; names, descriptions and Next are omitted as permitted.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook governs policy-tip UI on Mac, not the undocumented Mac wait-on-send setting.
claims.quote: To enable Policy Tip UI to appear in Outlook for Android, iOS, and macOS, you must enable the policy listed in the following section in the Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center.
claims.fix: Add: 'The current platform reference documents Mac policy tips, although the troubleshooting article Resolve issues that affect DLP policy tips still says policy tips are not supported for Outlook for Mac/iOS.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/troubleshoot/microsoft-365/data-loss-prevention/data-loss-prevention-policy-tips#client-doesn't-support-mailtips for that conflicting statement; keep the platform-specific reference as the basis for the control.

claims.claim: The policy-tips policy can target individuals or groups.
claims.quote: You can target policies to individuals or groups, so you can test and deploy policy tip UI as needed through your organization.

claims.claim: Learn documents no API for setting the Microsoft 365 Apps policy that enables Outlook policy-tip UI.
claims.quote: Searched: "Enable Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policy tips in Outlook" API Graph PowerShell; Microsoft 365 Apps cloud policy service API policy configuration Graph policy tips Outlook. Opened mobile reference and Cloud Policy creation/management excerpts; no setting API.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies reaches the policies used for the pre-send dialog configuration.
claims.quote: Sign in to the [Microsoft Purview portal](https://purview.microsoft.com) > **Data loss prevention** > **Policies**
claims.fix: The path stops at the policies list. Extend it using the cited creation route: 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom (Categories) > Custom (Regulations) > Full directory (Admin units) > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only)'. The note should say User notifications must be On.

claims.claim: The abbreviated New-DlpComplianceRule call uses the documented warn-rule parameters and values.
claims.quote: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <DLP Rule Name> -Policy <DLP Policy Name> -NotifyUser Owner -NotifyPolicyTipDisplayOption "Dialog" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation

claims.claim: The cited pre-send dialog instructions do not confirm Mac oversharing-dialog support.
claims.quote: Searched: Outlook Mac DLP wait on send default licensing timeout configuration. Opened dlp-osp-get-started and dlp-outlook-mobile-policy-tip-ref; the setup specifies Outlook for Microsoft 365 and the mobile oversharing section specifies Android/iOS, not Mac.

claims.claim: The full New-DlpComplianceRule example reproduces Learn's warn-rule label-condition structure, notification options and trusted-domain exception.
claims.quote: -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{operator = "And"; groups = @(@{operator="Or";name="Default";labels=@(@{name=<Label GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})})}) -ExceptIfRecipientDomainIs @("contoso.com","microsoft.com")

claims.claim: The Label GUID placeholder identifies the sensitivity label used by the condition.
claims.quote:
Configures one or more sensitivity label conditions. This sample includes one. At least one label is mandatory.

labels=@(@{name=<Label GUID>;type="Sensitivity"})
